title: 12 Best Craft Beer Bars in New York
description: The best craft beer bars in NYC — curated from Reddit reviews. Other Half, Tørst, Grimm, Blind Tiger, KCBC, Threes Brewing & more.

picks.name: Other Half Brewing Company
picks.insiderTip: The Domino Park location in Williamsburg has draft-only, taproom-exclusive offerings including low-ABV corn lagers and experimental pale ales you can't get anywhere else.
picks.verdict: The brewery that changed the East Coast hazy IPA game. Non-negotiable first stop.

picks.name: TØRST
picks.insiderTip: The rare bottle list is worth exploring if you want to splurge. Late-night hours until 1 AM on Fri/Sat.
picks.verdict: The sleekest craft beer bar in NYC — 21 rotating taps of rare brews in a stunning Greenpoint space.

picks.name: Grimm Artisanal Ales
picks.insiderTip: They dedicate 160 oak barrels to aging sour beer — unheard of in NYC. Buy freshly canned brews to take home.
picks.verdict: A husband-and-wife operation with a world-class sour program.

picks.name: Blind Tiger Ale House
picks.insiderTip: Open until 4 AM every night. Check weekly events for tap takeovers and cask nights.
picks.verdict: The most important craft beer bar in NYC history — where the city's craft beer culture was born.

picks.name: Finback Brooklyn
picks.insiderTip: The Brooklyn studio focuses on small-batch experiments, classic styles, and low-ABV session beers — a deliberate contrast to their Queens factory.
picks.verdict: Highest-rated brewery on the list at 4.8★. Founded by an architect and graphic artist.

picks.name: Threes Brewing
picks.insiderTip: Their pilsners and lagers are underrated gems. Functions as a café during the day with great coffee.
picks.verdict: The most versatile spot — brewery, café, and event space in 5,000 square feet.

picks.name: Kings County Brewers Collective (KCBC)
picks.insiderTip: Great outdoor space, regularly hosts food pop-ups. Buy 4-packs to go — well-priced for the quality.
picks.verdict: Bushwick's answer to the Gowanus brewery scene — where actual Brooklynites drink.

picks.name: Wild East Brewing Co.
picks.insiderTip: Their Czech and German-style lagers are a revelation in a city dominated by IPAs.
picks.verdict: The brewery that Finback's co-founder and multiple beer writers independently named as their top pick.

picks.name: Evil Twin Brewing NYC
picks.insiderTip: Same owner as Tørst. Check Instagram for special releases — they churn out an absurd number of unique beers.
picks.verdict: Denmark's most prolific gypsy brewer's NYC home base — creative, boundary-pushing beers.

picks.name: Covenhoven
picks.insiderTip: The grilled cheese sandwiches are a sleeper hit. Great bottle/can selection from hard-to-find NYC breweries.
picks.verdict: The quintessential neighborhood craft beer bar — no pretension, just great beer and good vibes.

picks.name: Proletariat
picks.insiderTip: Only 10 rotating drafts and ~30 bottles — every beer has been deliberately chosen. Expect rarities.
picks.verdict: The antithesis of a big brewery taproom — ten stools, ten drafts, eccentric curation.

picks.name: Spuyten Duyvil
picks.insiderTip: Only 6 drafts and 1 cask — the real treasure is the 100+ bottle list of European microbrews. The leafy backyard is one of the best outdoor drinking spots in Williamsburg.
picks.verdict: A Williamsburg classic that guarantees freshness by limiting to six drafts — the bottle collection is world-class.
